title: Isolation Good or Bad
summary: Isolation cuts you off from the outer world, decreases power, distorts your perspective, and leaves you vulnerable to plots and threats. Power is proportional to your contacts and active social interactions, which build security, trust, and awareness. To maintain control, one must actively interact with people, gather information, and avoid withdrawing into isolation.
example: A ferocious Chinese ruler built a secret-passage fortress and isolated himself out of fear, causing him to lose control of his empire and eventually die by poisoning.
An artist named Jacopo isolated himself for years to prevent others from stealing his fresco ideas, but without external criticism, his finished work turned out disproportionate.
King Louis XIV built Versailles to stay constantly surrounded by courtiers, allowing him to keep eyes on everything and prevent secrets from brewing.
French foreign minister Talleyrand actively connected with as many people as possible to gather information, allowing him to survive multiple transitions of power.
Cicero managed a balanced communication network between allies and enemies to maintain power.
reversal: Isolation should only be used as a last resort for short durations when seeking clarity amidst extreme ambiguity, but must be approached with caution because it is hard to recover from.
